trip_summary: A 4-day Belgium trip focusing on Brussels' Grand Place and Art Nouveau architecture plus Bruges' medieval charm, with strategic beer tastings and Belgian cuisine throughout.

key_decisions.decision: Base in Brussels both nights, day-trip to Bruges on Day 2
key_decisions.reasoning: Train between Brussels-Bruges takes roughly 1 hour and runs frequently (typically €15-20 return), making a day trip more cost-effective than changing hotels for a 4-day trip
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Splitting accommodation (2 nights Brussels, 1 Bruges) adds packing/checkout overhead and hotel costs without meaningful benefit for this duration

key_decisions.decision: Dedicate full Day 2 to Bruges, early departure
key_decisions.reasoning: Bruges is compact and walkable; a full day allows thorough exploration of Markt, canals, brewery visit, and return without rushing
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Half-day to Bruges would miss either the brewery culture aspect or proper canal exploration

key_decisions.reasoning: Atomium (typically €15pp) offers limited value for architecture/food interests; EU Quarter is office buildings that don't align with medieval/Art Nouveau focus
key_decisions.alternative_considered: These are Brussels classics but don't match stated interests and eat budget without clear payoff

key_decisions.reasoning: Allows proper Belgian cuisine experience (moules-frites, carbonnade) without blowing budget; lunch can be waffles/frites to balance
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Cheaper meals possible but would sacrifice core food interest; more expensive risks budget overrun

key_decisions.reasoning: These areas offer better value (typically €80-100/night for couples) than city center, with excellent Art Nouveau architecture and local restaurants within walking distance
key_decisions.alternative_considered: Grand Place area commands premium (€130+) without proportional benefit for moderate-pace travelers

items.title: Arrival to Brussels (airport or train)
items.location: Brussels Airport or Gare du Midi
items.reasoning: Assuming transport to Brussels covered separately; budget €10-12 for airport train if flying in

items.title: Check-in to hotel (3 nights)
items.reasoning: 3 nights at roughly €90-95/night in these neighborhoods balances budget, Art Nouveau surroundings, and metro access

items.title: Lunch at local friterie
items.reasoning: Belgian frites with stoofvlees sauce is iconic, cheap, and energizes afternoon walking; Place Jourdan has well-regarded options

items.title: Grand Place and guild houses
items.reasoning: UNESCO site and Belgium's most important architectural ensemble; free to visit, ideal orientation point for first afternoon

items.title: Beer tasting at Delirium Café or Moeder Lambic
items.location: Impasse de la Fidélité or Saint-Gilles
items.reasoning: Delirium has 2000+ beers (tourist-heavy but comprehensive); Moeder Lambic offers curated Belgian selection in authentic setting; roughly €5-7 per beer

items.title: Dinner: moules-frites
items.reasoning: Classic Belgian dish; €25-30pp at traditional brasseries gets full meal with house wine; touristy but reliable execution

items.title: Train Brussels to Bruges
items.reasoning: Early train (roughly 1 hour) maximizes Bruges time; return ticket typically €15-20pp with advance booking

items.title: Markt square and Belfry (exterior)
items.reasoning: Medieval market square with guild halls; climbing Belfry (€12) optional but crowds may not justify cost for moderate-pace trip

items.title: Canal walk to Beguinage
items.reasoning: Bruges' defining feature is medieval canals; Beguinage (small entry fee, roughly €3) offers tranquil courtyard and architecture

items.title: Lunch: waterzooi or Flemish stew
items.reasoning: Regional dish (chicken/fish waterzooi); €15-18pp at mid-range spot balances authenticity and budget

items.title: De Halve Maan Brewery tour
items.reasoning: Only active brewery in Bruges center; tour (roughly €14pp) includes history, rooftop view, and tasting; core to beer culture interest

items.title: Minnewater and walk back to station
items.reasoning: Picturesque lake and park; allows gentle transition to departure while seeing southern Bruges

items.title: Train Bruges to Brussels
items.reasoning: Return leg included in morning ticket cost

items.title: Light dinner: waffles or cheese/charcuterie
items.reasoning: After full Bruges day and lunch, lighter evening meal keeps budget in check; Belgian waffles (€8-10) or shared plate works

days.feasibility_flag: 6 activities/meals scheduled in one day — likely overpacked, review pacing.

items.title: Art Nouveau architecture walk: Horta Museum area
items.reasoning: Horta Museum (€10-15 entry) showcases Art Nouveau master; surrounding streets have Hankar and other townhouses; aligns perfectly with architecture interest

items.title: Lunch: Brussels waffle and coffee
items.location: Authentic waffle shop (avoid tourist traps near Manneken Pis)
items.reasoning: Light lunch to save budget for dinner; genuine Brussels waffle (Liège-style, €5-6) from local spot plus coffee

items.title: Sablon antiques quarter and Notre-Dame du Sablon church
items.reasoning: Elegant square with Gothic church (free entry), chocolate shops (browsing free), and weekend antiques if applicable; architectural merit without cost

items.title: Belgian Beer World or Cantillon Brewery
items.reasoning: Beer World (€10pp, central) is interactive museum; Cantillon (€9pp) is working lambic brewery with tasting; Cantillon wins for authenticity and beer culture depth

items.title: Dinner: carbonnade flamande or Belgian classics
items.reasoning: Flemish beef stew or other regional dish; €30-35pp at quality brasserie with beer pairing; final night warrants fuller meal

items.title: Marolles flea market (if Sunday) or Comic Strip Walk
items.location: Place du Jeu de Balle or city center murals
items.reasoning: Marolles market (Sunday) offers local flavor and vintage finds; otherwise comic murals are free outdoor art aligned with Belgian culture; coffee budget €5

items.title: Hotel checkout
items.reasoning: Standard checkout time; allows morning activity before departure

items.title: Lunch: speculoos and coffee or light bite
items.reasoning: Final Belgian treat before leaving; speculoos cookies with coffee or small sandwich; keeps budget intact

items.title: Departure from Brussels
items.reasoning: Transport out assumed separate from trip budget; timing depends on departure method

things_to_skip.reasoning: €15pp entry for 1958 Expo structure doesn't align with medieval/Art Nouveau architecture focus; peripheral location (30min+ from center) eats time and metro budget
Tourist attraction with miniatures doesn't match stated interests in authentic architecture and food culture; €18pp better spent on actual beer/food experiences
Modern office buildings (European Parliament, Commission) don't serve architecture interest; tours require advance booking and don't align with food/beer culture priorities
€12-15pp for 30min boat tour is pleasant but walking the canals is free and equally photogenic; budget better allocated to brewery tour which combines beer interest with experience
€10-15pp for museum or €50+ for workshop; browsing actual chocolatiers (Sablon area) gives cultural exposure without major cost; interests prioritize beer over chocolate
Only open July-September, so unavailable in October; exterior and park are free alternatives if passing through
